subject.title: fix(models): clear stale auth cooldowns after early limit resets

question: Should OpenClaw support `models auth clear-cooldown <profile-id>` as the explicit operator escape hatch for early provider recovery, rather than requiring a Doctor/in-product recovery action or relying only on automatic probes?
rationale: The locked persistence implementation is mechanically reviewable, but a new public command that changes saved provider eligibility is a durable product and support contract decision.

options.title: Adopt the explicit reset
options.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI command after redacted real-flow proof confirms it clears only the intended state and the next request recovers safely.

options.title: Use guided recovery
options.body: Pause this command and place the reset behind Doctor or an in-product recovery surface for users who cannot safely operate a terminal.

options.title: Rely on automatic recovery
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers want early recovery handled exclusively through provider probes and fallback policy rather than manual state mutation.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit reset
recommendation.body: Approve the profile-scoped CLI command after redacted real-flow proof confirms it clears only the intended state and the next request recovers safely.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history ties steipete to the central auth-profile refactor and related cooldown-state corrections, making this the strongest available routing signal.
